assessmentSummary.identity: Seated Straddle Reach-to-Tall is one bodyweight cycle: begin in a tall seated straddle on a stable floor or mat, reach forward through a comfortable controllable range without forcing a passive hold, then return to the same tall seated straddle before the next repetition. It is not a static pancake stretch, any leg lift or compression drill, a pike fold, a supine trunk lift, a loaded mobility drill, or an assessment.
currentCardFindings: Source 74 conflates a forward reach with unspecified one- or two-leg lifts and both upright and folded trunks; those actions have different support, count, loading, fatigue, and safety contracts.

The exact reach-to-tall cycle is sufficiently defined to become a review-only candidate. The leg-lift fragment remains quarantined because the source does not state hand support, lift laterality, knee position, lift/lower count unit, or contact boundary; it is not silently mapped to the existing Seated Compression Lift.
Three search-discovered direct YouTube URLs are candidates only. Search-result visibility is not playback, exact-cycle, accessibility, quality, reviewer, or approval verification.

proposedLoadProfile.recovery: candidate planning estimate only; recompute from actual range, repetitions, tempo, symptoms, and overlapping trunk, hip, or adductor work

proposedDosage.prepare: 1-3 short quality-limited sets of exact reach-to-tall cycles
proposedDosage.tempo: slow forward reach, deliberate tall return, and reset between repetitions
proposedDosage.rest: restore breathing, tall posture, and absence of symptoms before the next set
proposedDosage.durationRule: include floor setup, demonstration, repetitions, tall resets, rest, substitutions, cleaning, and exit

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Select only when the exact seated-straddle forward-reach-to-tall contract, floor access, communication, current range, symptoms, fatigue budget, and downstream work fit. Changing leg position, knee position, hand support, range, tempo, static hold, lifting, external load, intent, or substitution reruns selection, logistics, duration, fatigue, relationships, and validation.

calibrationEvidence.basis: Source 74 lineage, dynamic-stretching evidence, safe gymnastics instruction, task mechanics, and comparison with static straddle stretching, leg lifts/compression, pike fold, and loaded mobility tasks.
calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: Evidence does not establish universal range, repetitions, tempo, recovery, readiness, symptom interpretation, clearance, outcome, or Vortex score. Independent human calibration remains required.
